description:
# Compliance ticket for opi-q5k.15

Source check: opi-q5k.15 (select-list.test.ts audit)

## Implementation

Upgrade `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/select_list.ex` from the current MVP (items = `[String.t()]`) to match upstream semantics:

### Item struct
Items become `%SelectList.Item{value: any, label: String.t(), description: String.t() | nil}`. Accept plain strings as a convenience that auto-wrap into `%Item{value: s, label: s, description: nil}` to avoid breaking existing callers.

### Render semantics (matching tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/src/components/select-list.ts)
- Two-column layout: primary (label) column + description column, separated by spaces.
- Primary column width is:
  - at least `min_primary_column_width` (default 0),
  - at most `max_primary_column_width` (default large),
  - otherwise the natural width of the widest label (visible_width).
- Labels longer than the effective primary width are truncated via a truncation hook (default: ANSI-aware trim ending in `"..."` via `WrapAnsi.truncate_to_width` from opi-q5k.31).
- Description column starts at the same absolute column for every row (alignment preserved even when labels were truncated).
- Multiline descriptions are normalized to a single line by replacing `\n` with `" "` before rendering.
- Theme protocol fields: `selectedPrefix`, `selectedText`, `description`, `scrollInfo`, `noMatch` — functions that receive text and return styled text. Expose as a `%Theme{}` struct or `[callback_*: fun]` keyword — follow project convention (check existing theme handling, e.g., in apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/theme.ex if it exists).

### Options
- `min_primary_column_width :: non_neg_integer()`
- `max_primary_column_width :: non_neg_integer()`
- `truncate_primary :: ({text, max_width} -> text) | nil` — custom truncation hook

### Backwards compatibility
Preserve existing keyboard handling (handle_key for Up/Down/Enter/Escape, wrapping, empty-list no-op). Preserve existing tests in select_list_test.exs.

## Dependencies
- Soft-depends on opi-q5k.31 (WrapAnsi.truncate_to_width).
- Blocks opi-q5k.1 (acceptance gate).

## Tests to port to select_list_test.exs

1. Multiline description normalization:
   ```
   items = [%Item{value: "test", label: "test", description: "Line one\nLine two\nLine three"}]
   list = %SelectList{items: items, selected: 5}
   rendered = SelectList.render(list, 100)
   assert length(rendered) > 0
   refute String.contains?(hd(rendered), "\n")
   assert String.contains?(hd(rendered), "Line one Line two Line three")
   ```

2. Descriptions aligned when primary text is truncated:
   - items: short-label + very-long-label, both with descriptions
   - render at width 80
   - assert `visible_index_of(row0, "short description") == visible_index_of(row1, "long description")`
   (where `visible_index_of` counts visible_width of prefix to the target text — mirror upstream helper.)

3. Minimum primary column width:
   - items with labels "a" and "bb"
   - options: `min_primary_column_width: 12, max_primary_column_width: 20`
   - descriptions "first" and "second" both start at column 14 (i.e., `String.slice` at 14 starts "first"/"second").

4. Maximum primary column width:
   - items: very-long-label (44 chars) + short-label
   - same options
   - descriptions "first" and "second" both start at column 22 (long label truncated to 20, then 2-column gap).

5. Custom truncation hook preserves alignment:
   - options: `min_primary_column_width: 12, max_primary_column_width: 12, truncate_primary: fn %{text: t, max_width: m} -> if String.length(t) <= m, do: t, else: String.slice(t, 0, max(0, m - 1)) <> "…"`
   - assert rendered row for long label contains `"…"`
   - assert descriptions for long + short rows start at the same visible column

Port the `visible_index_of` helper: given a line and a target substring, returns the visible_width of the portion before the target. Upstream implementation is at select-list.test.ts:14-18 — replicate in Elixir using `OctoPi.TUI.WrapAnsi.visible_width/1` on the slice before the match.

## Re-comparison (required)

After implementation + tests land, re-read tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/select-list.test.ts and confirm every `it(...)` block has an Elixir equivalent. Post a final comment here before closing.

comments.text: Done. SelectList.Item struct + two-column layout + truncate_primary hook. All 5 upstream parity tests pass alongside existing 10 keyboard tests. Natural width formula matches upstream (visible_width + PRIMARY_COLUMN_GAP(2)) clamped to [min, max].

title: Upgrade SelectList to {value,label,description} items + port select-list.test.ts (5 tests)
